body:
CANDIDATE bd-01M15R1K434JHHJWKNGHTYKDP3: 4d98c0f on branch m1/leakage, parent current main 31cccb2. Law I5 clause 4 - the fame-by-channel leakage control - is now IMPLEMENTED rather than merely required. Four files: new bench/leakage.scala and LeakageSuite.scala, plus channels.scala and report.scala for the exposure field.

WHY I DID THIS UNPROMPTED: clause 4 says the control is mandatory before any default is selected, and nothing in the harness computed it. That is exactly the lag between a law and its enforcement you caught me on an hour ago, one clause to the left. I would rather find the second instance myself than have you find it.

WHAT IT COMPUTES. Within a channel: mean on high-risk stories minus mean on low-risk stories. Then subtract the same contrast averaged over the NON-MEMORIZING channels. What survives is the channel-specific advantage - "famous stories are simply easier for everyone" cancels, and only "this channel does better exactly where summaries exist" remains. ChannelExposure (Memorizing | NonMemorizing) is DECLARED on the channel, never inferred from a provider fingerprint string, per your ruling on the grakern receipt seam: no implicit default, the caller wiring the channel is the one who knows.

NotApplicable is a first-class verdict with a reason, not a pass: no high-risk story in the probe, or no non-memorizing channel to subtract, means the control measured NOTHING - and "no evidence" must never render as "no leakage". Only memorizing channels can be flagged; a baseline that happens to soar on famous stories moves the subtrahend, it does not accuse itself.

MUTATION PROOF, three mutants, each alone, each reverted, gate green after: L1 stop subtracting the baseline gain -> the uniform-fame test FAILS (every channel including both baselines is flagged, which is the false-positive machine the subtraction exists to prevent). L2 return Clear instead of NotApplicable when no baseline exists -> "never a silent pass" FAILS. L3 ignore exposure when flagging -> "a baseline does not implicate itself" FAILS.

EVIDENCE at 4d98c0f, clean pin, and this time the gate was the LAST action before commit from the exact committed tree, per the rule I adopted after my scalafmt regression: embedBench 37/37 (was 29; eight new), compileAll success on all three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll success, scalafmtSbtCheck success. Working tree clean but for the sbt shim.

A COHERENCE PROBLEM IN THE LAW I WROTE, which I found while implementing and would rather raise than paper over: clause 3 keeps high-risk stories OUT of any set that may be labelled calibrated, so a calibrated set can never contain the high arm this control needs. The control is therefore, by construction, an instrument for a DIAGNOSTIC probe deliberately mixing risk levels - its verdict is evidence about a CHANNEL, not about a set. That is coherent and I have documented it that way, but it leaves clause 4's "before any default is selected" without an enforcement hook: today nothing requires that a channel eligible for a default has actually passed a leakage probe. The natural fix is a precondition on Calibrated - each memorizing channel names a passed probe by receipt checksum - but that is a law-shaped change to what calibrated MEANS, and after this evening I am not making one of those unilaterally at 4am. Your ruling; if you want it, it is a small commit on top of this one and I will bring the mutation proof.
